text.title: Micro-MVPs Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Micro-MVPs. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

rule.statement: Scope ≤5 dev-days; exceeds = re-cut with the rubric.
rule.rationale: Scope ≤5 dev-days; exceeds = re-cut with the rubric.

rule.statement: One Micro-MVP tests one assumption; multi-risk = split.
rule.rationale: One Micro-MVP tests one assumption; multi-risk = split.

rule.statement: Both kill and success thresholds named before ship.
rule.rationale: Both kill and success thresholds named before ship.

rule.statement: ≥1 Micro-MVP shipped per cycle (2 weeks); 0 = methodology not running.
rule.rationale: ≥1 Micro-MVP shipped per cycle (2 weeks); 0 = methodology not running.

rule.statement: Match the experiment type to the assumption category. Do not build a landing page to validate willingness-to-pay; use a smoke test instead.
rule.rationale: Each experiment type has a different signal type. Using the wrong type wastes time and produces misleading data. Pick from the catalogue in the section below.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-micro-mvps.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.

section.title: Experiment catalogue
section.p: Six micro-MVP experiment types mapped to effort range and what each one validates. Rule r6-match-experiment-type selects from this list.

list.item: Landing page (1 day): validates demand and messaging. Shows a description of the product and measures sign-up rate or email capture.
Concierge (1 week): validates workflow and core value. Manually deliver the product's promise to 5–10 users to discover the real job-to-be-done.
Wizard of Oz (days): validates UX and willingness-to-pay. Fake automated product backed by manual human fulfilment; users interact as if it is real.
Video demo (hours): validates interest and virality. Record the product promise; measure views, shares, and comments before building anything.
Fake door (hours): validates feature demand. Add a button or menu item for a feature that does not exist yet; measure click rate before building.
Smoke test (days): validates price sensitivity and conversion. Offer the product for purchase; measure conversion at the target price point before delivering.
